findings.text: A newcomer learns in one paragraph what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. This part works well.
findings.source: Opening paragraph under the h1: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The title is about a different project. A newcomer who came to Athena's own site meets a study of 'firstmate', a tool they have probably never heard of, so it takes a few paragraphs to work out which project the page is really about.

The one section meant to show Athena's main promise (models, verdict and cost traced to a request) is the first section after the navigation, and it shows a failure. It also repeats the error text. This undercuts the pitch right where a newcomer looks for proof.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link is aimed at the project owner, not a visitor, yet it sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. It is confusing to someone meeting the page for the first time.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Even the default 'core' track is full of firstmate internals: exit codes, guarded fast-forwards, pending-close records, stale wakes. A newcomer gets little from it about Athena beyond 'it can produce a detailed, sourced reading'.
findings.source: Start here: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: Being honest about gaps is good, but many definitions say the term is undefined. For a newcomer this reads as noise rather than help.
findings.source: Glossary entries such as "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat." and "in scope ... this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: Next steps are clear and concrete: a prerequisites list, install commands, and a one-line example (athena ask "add a changelog"). The 'cd athena' step between clone and setup is missing. The page does not say whether Rust or cargo must be installed beforehand, or whether Claude Code needs an account.
findings.source: Next steps: "Get the code: git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" then "Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh"

findings.text: The header links straight to the next steps, so a newcomer can skip the long study and still find out how to try Athena.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" (header link to #next-steps)

findings.text: This is a detail of how the site is built, and it means nothing to a visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
